title: Partial-emission reconciliation, stream boundary guarantees, and idempotent tool-call contract
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Purpose: Define clear, testable acceptance criteria for how the Redwood API and Console handle partially-emitted structured outputs when interleaved with tool/function calls. This ticket captures the expected semantics for: schema version negotiation, stream framing and checkpoints, non-fatal vs fatal error tokens, idempotent tool invocation, and reconciliation of partial state after client or network interruptions.

Background: Customers have started integrating long-running streamed responses with multi-step tool orchestration. We need deterministic behavior when a client disconnects mid-stream, when a model decides to emit a tool call, or when downstream services return errors. Existing docs cover streaming schemas and fallback modes, but none specify reconciliation steps, idempotency guarantees for tool handlers, or the exact token-level error semantics required by infra and SDK teams.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Schema negotiation: the server MUST include a 'schema_version' field in the initial stream preamble and the client may provide an 'accepted_versions' header. If version mismatch, server emits a single 'schema_mismatch' control event and follows the fallback policy described below.

2) Stream framing and checkpoints: all streamed structured outputs MUST include optional 'checkpoint' events every N tokens (N configurable via route). A checkpoint contains an offset integer and a canonical digest of the last emitted structured object. Checkpoints are advisory but required for reconcilers when 'resume' is requested.

3) Partial-emission reconciliation: if client disconnects and later resumes with a 'resume_token' (last checkpoint digest + offset), the server MUST resume the stream from the next logical token or emit a 'reconcile' control event explaining dropped tokens. No duplicate application-visible tool calls should be delivered to the same idempotency key (see #5).

4) Error token classes: the stream MUST distinguish between 'nonfatal_error' (metadata-only; stream continues) and 'fatal_error' (terminates the stream with an error code and optional partial_result pointer). Nonfatal errors MUST include a 'recoverability' field with values: none | retryable | degraded. Clients and Console tooling will surface nonfatal errors inline without closing the stream.

5) Tool-call idempotency: for each tool call emitted in-stream the client SDK MUST send an Idempotency-Key header when invoking the tool backend. The server must expose a canonical idempotency-key in the tool-call event (uuid v4). Repeat deliveries of the same idempotency-key to a downstream tool MUST result in at-most-once application semantics (server-level deduplication or tool-backend honor).

6) Backpressure and partial body semantics: streaming routes MUST implement a soft backpressure hint (window size) in the preamble. If downstream backpressure breaches high-water mark, server emits 'backpressure_applied' control events and may buffer up to the configured limit. If buffer overflow occurs, server MUST emit a 'buffer_overflow' nonfatal_error with recoverability: degraded and continue with a reduced-quality/shortened object if configured.

7) Tool-call fallback modes: if a real-time tool invocation fails with a transient error, the server MAY fallback to 'deferred-invocation' mode where it returns a placeholder tool-result object and schedules a background retry. The stream must emit 'deferred_invocation_scheduled' control event and expose a lookup id that clients can poll.

8) Metrics and observability: each stream must be annotated with trace_id, stream_start_ts, stream_end_ts (if ended), number_of_checkpoints, number_of_tool_calls, number_of_nonfatal_errors. These fields are required for Console dashboards and must appear in final summary control event on normal termination.

9) Compatibility: older clients that do not support checkpoints must still be able to consume streams; server MUST send a compact, single-message fallback that summarizes partial structured output when resume is impossible.
test_plan:
- Integration test: start a long-running streamed response with 3 checkpoints; simulate client disconnect after second checkpoint; resume using resume_token and assert no duplicate tool invocations and that reconciliation event is emitted.
- Unit test: emit nonfatal_error tokens interleaved with valid object emissions; assert client SDK surfaces inline errors and continues processing.
- Chaos test: induce transient tool-backend failures; verify server emits deferred_invocation_scheduled and that lookup id resolves to final result after retry.
- Load test: stream with high-frequency checkpoints (N=50) under heavy concurrency; verify metrics are emitted and Console summary matches counters.
- Security test: validate that idempotency-key cannot be forged to replay tool results for other users; run RBAC/permission checks on lookup id access.
rollback_plan:
If issues appear in canary: 1) roll back streaming schema change via feature flag to previous stable preamble (schema_version X), 2) disable automatic checkpointing for affected routes, 3) block deferred-invocation fallbacks and require sync tool failures to surface as fatal_error to ensure easier debugging. Engage on-call infra and notify customers with active canary usage.

Post-mortem: capture the timeline, reproduce with deterministic seed, and schedule a hotfix if more than 5% of canary streams hit duplicate-tool-call events.
decisions_log:
- Agreed: Use explicit checkpoint events instead of implicit token counts for easier reconciliation in the Console.
- Agreed: Emit both idempotency-key in event and require client-side Idempotency-Key header to downstream tool calls to ensure cross-process dedupe.
- Rejected: Using HTTP/2 stream resets as primary resume mechanism (too brittle across SDKs).
- Pending: exact default checkpoint frequency (engineering to propose sane default based on latency/cost tradeoffs).
